text-theme-text-sec text-pretty leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Salesforce is a Software company in North America.</p><div class="not-prose mb-8 mb-0 mt-v1"><div class="pb-g1.75"><div class="border-theme-border-02 flex flex-col gap-v1 border-l-2 pl-g1.5 pb-[2px]"><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">75%</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Salesforce engineering adoption</div></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">30%+</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">PR velocity increase</div></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">85%</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Less time on legacy test coverage</div></div></div></div></div></div></aside><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>Salesforce has been building software for more than 25 years. It maintains a codebase that stretches across decades featuring every kind of system a modern tech company can accumulate. Thousands of engineers across the globe ship new products on top of it every day.</p>
<p>That&#x27;s what makes the rapid adoption of Cursor inside Salesforce so notable. When an organization this central to the industry shifts how it builds software, it points at where the whole field is heading.</p>
<p>Today, thousands of engineers at Salesforce use Cursor as part of their daily workflow. Salesforce has already seen double-digit gains in velocity and code quality.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">I would say that it&#x27;s 0 to 1 in terms of how Cursor has transformed the way our developers use tools to improve quality of the product.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="two-paths-toward-cursor-adoption" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#two-paths-toward-cursor-adoption" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Two paths toward Cursor adoption</h2>
<p>Before Cursor arrived, Salesforce had already invested in its own internal AI tools. But Salesforce wanted its engineers to have a range of options, so it made Cursor available.</p>
<p>Junior engineers were the first adopters. Many had started their careers during the pandemic, when remote work made standard ways of learning a codebase unavailable. Cursor helped them catch up.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">They didn&#x27;t have senior engineers sitting with them and explaining a lot of things. Cursor helps them actually understand existing code better so that they are able to contribute more effectively.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<p>For senior engineers, Appajodu observed that they first proved out Cursor on the boring, tedious tasks that are inefficient to tackle manually. And as they experienced the value of automating these tasks and built trust in the tool, these senior engineers expanded their use cases quickly to higher value tasks.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Senior engineers start with the places that feel boring, and once they see the value there, they&#x27;re ready to use AI coding for other use cases.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<p>Adoption followed the same pattern across teams: a small group would try Cursor, see the impact, and the rest would follow. Within a few months, Cursor went from a new tool at Salesforce to one that was more widely used in day-to-day work. And over time, AI proliferated into every aspect of the SDLC, not just code writing, according to Appajodu.</p>
<h2 id="three-metrics-that-matter-most" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#three-metrics-that-matter-most" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Three metrics that matter most</h2>
<p>Salesforce is careful about how it evaluates engineering work. The company measures pace and reliability using three key metrics:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Cycle time</strong></li>
<li><strong>Quality (bug count)</strong></li>
<li><strong>Throughput</strong></li>
</ul>
<p>Salesforce already had dashboards that tracked these metrics across thousands of engineers, making the impact of Cursor visible almost immediately. Cursor helped Salesforce make large improvements in all three areas. One team at Salesforce also <a href="https://engineering.salesforce.com/how-cursor-ai-cut-legacy-code-coverage-time-by-85/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reduced legacy code coverage time by 85%</a>.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">We have seen more than double-digit increases in all of these metrics.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="shipping-better-products-than-ever" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#shipping-better-products-than-ever" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Shipping better products than ever</h2>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">We have seen a huge improvement in the quality of products.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<p>To take one measure, engineers are now generating far more unit tests with Cursor than before, enhancing the reliability of what Salesforce ships.</p>
<p>AI is already reshaping how software is planned, built, and maintained, and Appajodu believes the real transformation is still ahead: &quot;We are just at the starting point of the journey. It&#x27;s only going to get better.&quot;</p>
<hr/>
<p>If you&#x27;re interested in leveraging AI to ship higher-quality software, faster, please <a href="https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=customers" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reach out to our team</a> to get started with a Cursor trial.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- --> </span><a class="border-theme-border-02 flex flex-col gap-v1 border-l-2 pl-g1.5 pb-[2px]"><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">75%</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Salesforce engineering adoption</div></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">30%+</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">PR velocity increase</div></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-v2/12"><div class="type-md-lg text-theme-text">85%</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec leading-[var(--leading-cozy)]">Less time on legacy test coverage</div></div></div></div></div></div></aside><div class="prose prose--block prose--blog col-span-full! prose-dropcap"><p>Salesforce has been building software for more than 25 years. It maintains a codebase that stretches across decades featuring every kind of system a modern tech company can accumulate. Thousands of engineers across the globe ship new products on top of it every day.</p>
<p>That&#x27;s what makes the rapid adoption of Cursor inside Salesforce so notable. When an organization this central to the industry shifts how it builds software, it points at where the whole field is heading.</p>
<p>Today, thousands of engineers at Salesforce use Cursor as part of their daily workflow. Salesforce has already seen double-digit gains in velocity and code quality.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">I would say that it&#x27;s 0 to 1 in terms of how Cursor has transformed the way our developers use tools to improve quality of the product.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="two-paths-toward-cursor-adoption" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#two-paths-toward-cursor-adoption" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Two paths toward Cursor adoption</h2>
<p>Before Cursor arrived, Salesforce had already invested in its own internal AI tools. But Salesforce wanted its engineers to have a range of options, so it made Cursor available.</p>
<p>Junior engineers were the first adopters. Many had started their careers during the pandemic, when remote work made standard ways of learning a codebase unavailable. Cursor helped them catch up.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">They didn&#x27;t have senior engineers sitting with them and explaining a lot of things. Cursor helps them actually understand existing code better so that they are able to contribute more effectively.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<p>For senior engineers, Appajodu observed that they first proved out Cursor on the boring, tedious tasks that are inefficient to tackle manually. And as they experienced the value of automating these tasks and built trust in the tool, these senior engineers expanded their use cases quickly to higher value tasks.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">Senior engineers start with the places that feel boring, and once they see the value there, they&#x27;re ready to use AI coding for other use cases.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<p>Adoption followed the same pattern across teams: a small group would try Cursor, see the impact, and the rest would follow. Within a few months, Cursor went from a new tool at Salesforce to one that was more widely used in day-to-day work. And over time, AI proliferated into every aspect of the SDLC, not just code writing, according to Appajodu.</p>
<h2 id="three-metrics-that-matter-most" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#three-metrics-that-matter-most" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Three metrics that matter most</h2>
<p>Salesforce is careful about how it evaluates engineering work. The company measures pace and reliability using three key metrics:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Cycle time</strong></li>
<li><strong>Quality (bug count)</strong></li>
<li><strong>Throughput</strong></li>
</ul>
<p>Salesforce already had dashboards that tracked these metrics across thousands of engineers, making the impact of Cursor visible almost immediately. Cursor helped Salesforce make large improvements in all three areas. One team at Salesforce also <a href="https://engineering.salesforce.com/how-cursor-ai-cut-legacy-code-coverage-time-by-85/" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reduced legacy code coverage time by 85%</a>.</p>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">We have seen more than double-digit increases in all of these metrics.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<h2 id="shipping-better-products-than-ever" class="anchor-heading group "><a href="#shipping-better-products-than-ever" class="anchor-link" aria-label="Link to this section"><span class="anchor-icon" aria-hidden="true">#</span></a>Shipping better products than ever</h2>
<div class="not-prose my-6"><div class="card"><p class="type-base text-theme-text mb-6 whitespace-pre-line">We have seen a huge improvement in the quality of products.</p><div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text">Shan Appajodu</div><div class="type-sm text-theme-text-sec">SVP of Engineering, Salesforce</div></div></div></div>
<p>To take one measure, engineers are now generating far more unit tests with Cursor than before, enhancing the reliability of what Salesforce ships.</p>
<p>AI is already reshaping how software is planned, built, and maintained, and Appajodu believes the real transformation is still ahead: &quot;We are just at the starting point of the journey. It&#x27;s only going to get better.&quot;</p>
<hr/>
<p>If you&#x27;re interested in leveraging AI to ship higher-quality software, faster, please <a href="https://cursor.com/contact-sales?source=customers" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">reach out to our team</a> to get started with a Cursor trial.</p></div><footer class="mt-v2"><p class="type-base"><span class="text-theme-text-sec">Filed under:<!-- --> </span><a
